what: GE HealthCare makes medical imaging equipment: MRI, CT and ultrasound scanners, X-ray systems, patient monitors, and the contrast agents injected before scans. It was spun out of General Electric in 2023.
customers: Hospitals, imaging centres and health systems worldwide, plus pharmaceutical companies using its diagnostic agents.
money: MRI, CT, X-ray and molecular imaging systems
moat: An installed base of scanners in hospitals worldwide that generates service contracts and replacement sales for decades, plus contrast agent manufacturing that few can match.
risks: Chinese hospital purchasing has been weak and government procurement rules favour local suppliers
Debt of about $10 billion from the spin-off
Tariffs raise the cost of equipment built across borders
opportunities: Pharmaceutical diagnostics is a high-margin business with new Alzheimer's imaging agents
Service contracts on the installed base provide recurring revenue
Hospitals are replacing scanners installed a decade or more ago
watch: Order growth, especially in China, and pharmaceutical diagnostics revenue.
